item.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
item.description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Cataluña enfrenta lluvias e inundaciones récord mientras la alerta se traslada a Girona
item.description: Cataluña afronta las consecuencias de un temporal extraordinario que ha dejado lluvias torrenciales de más de 200 litros por metro cuadrado en algunas zonas, provocando inundaciones, daños en viviendas y afectaciones a negocios. Mientras vecinos evalúan las pérdidas y comienzan las labores de limpieza, las autoridades mantienen la alerta ante el avance del sistema meteorológico hacia el norte de la región. La provincia de Girona, fronteriza con Francia, concentra ahora la mayor preocupación, con avisos de riesgo y llamados a la población para que permanezca a salvo en sus viviendas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Hong Kong issues amber rainstorm warning
item.description: The Hong Kong Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning on Sunday evening, with the signal remaining in place for more than two hours. The weather forecaster issued the alert – the lowest level in a three-tier warning system – at 8.20pm and cancelled it at 10.30pm. “A few squally thunderstorms are expected to occur over Hong Kong,” a spokesman for the Observatory said in the evening. Showers would be heavy at times. The forecaster also warned that intense gusts reaching 70km/h (43mph) could... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: More than 1,200 Colorado students have earned a climate ‘seal’: ‘We’re the ones growing up in this world’
item.description: A statewide initiative pairs climate-focused coursework with community service – and is spreading to other states As a student at a high school not far from Denver’s main airport, Anthony Muñoz wondered whether the jet fuel from airplanes flying above his campus was harming living things. An avid gardener, Muñoz partnered with a local university to create a garden on the campus of his charter school, Vista Academy, filling it with native plants that could detect ground-level ozone pollution. He also worked with climate scientists from the National Center for Atmospheric Research, a federal… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Revealed: Government quietly dropped plan to prepare England for wildfires
item.description: FOI request shows wildfire risk scheme scrapped, as survey highlights many fire services lack proper protective gear The government quietly scrapped plans to prepare the countryside in England for wildfires, it has been revealed. This was despite new data showing fire crews do not have the proper protective gear to tackle them. This summer has been a potent reminder of the scale of the threat posed by the climate crisis, with the UK experiencing record-breaking wildfires after punishingly hot and dry weather turned large parts of the countryside into a tinderbox. item.title: Indonesians sue president over haze – can it clear the air?
item.description: For months, the air over West Kalimantan has been thick enough to taste. Now, some of the province’s residents are taking the government to court over it. Indonesia’s worst wildfire season in 11 years has been sending plumes of toxic haze drifting across borders to Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines since at least August. But nowhere has been worse hit than West Kalimantan, where more than 48,000 hectares (185 square miles) of land and forest have burned since the start of the year,... item.title: Four North Carolina homes repaired after Helene face demolition after FEMA buyouts
item.description: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. To address the persistent flood threats, homeowners have chosen FEMA's voluntary buyouts, aligning with the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program's initiative to convert affected land into green spaces, thereby reducing future flood risks. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Queensland dairy farmer opened four campsites after drought forced her family to sell 40 cows
item.description: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: When the atmosphere slows the Earth: Uncovering a subtle signal of climate change
item.description: Atmospheric circulation governs weather and climate, but it also carries angular momentum. When winds shift or mass redistributes, the atmosphere can exchange momentum with the solid Earth, slightly altering the planet's rotation rate. This is not a new concept, but what happens under long-term global warming? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Georgia begins 10-year forest restoration at 132-acre Towaliga Preserve with data-centre partnership
item.description: The Towaliga Preserve is about to launch an ambitious 10-year forest restoration project, backed by QTS Data Centres. This significant initiative aims to revitalize 132 acres, focusing on ecosystem management and biodiversity enhancement. Throughout the decade, contractors will engage in tasks like invasive species control and planting native trees. After the project, the Southern Conservation Trust will ensure the area remains cared for and healthy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: En 1974, Francia necesitaba evitar que París volviera a inundarse. La solución fue tan sencilla como radical: borrar tres pueblos del mapa
item.description: La gran inundación de París de 1910 dejó una imagen difícil de olvidar: calles convertidas en canales, vecinos desplazándose en barca y el Sena alcanzando 8,62 metros en el puente de Austerlitz. Francia necesitaba impedir que una crecida semejante volviera a golpear la capital y terminó adoptando una solución a una escala gigantesca. A unos 190 kilómetros de París construyó un depósito capaz de almacenar 350 millones de metros cúbicos de agua. El problema era que en el lugar elegido ya había algo: bosques, campos y tres pueblos enteros. Algo donde guardar agua. El problema no era únicamente… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: 57 new deep-sea species discovered in Argentina’s Mar del Plata Canyon, including ‘Loki’ sea cucumber
item.description: In a groundbreaking deep-sea voyage off Argentina, scientists uncovered 57 brand new marine species alongside five previously unclassified genera. Using a remotely operated vehicle, they pulled samples from the Mar del Plata Submarine Canyon. Among these marine marvels was a unique and translucent sea cucumber whimsically dubbed Loki. A subsequent collaborative workshop was instrumental in accelerating the species identification process, highlighting the astonishing biodiversity of the South Atlantic's deep ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: A Moroccan mine built a road from phosphate waste rock; field tests cut dust emissions by 91%
item.description: In Morocco, a phosphate mine has implemented an innovative road surface made from waste rock generated during phosphate extraction. This robust, three-layered pavement design not only successfully supports heavy mining vehicles but also helps manage dust emissions effectively. Testing resulted in a notable decrease in airborne dust and enhanced road quality, with an anticipated 15 percent boost in productivity for mining operations, while also cutting down maintenance expenses. item.title: The expansion of Heathrow would be an expensive disaster for Britain and the world. Burnham needs to block it | George Monbiot
item.description: A third runway would fly in the face of reason. If we are to prioritise human life over short-term ‘growth’, we need to use planes less, not more If a third runway is built at Heathrow, what will be the impact on the wealth of the nation? It will cost us somewhere between £23.4bn and £62.5bn. These are not my figures ; they weren’t calculated by environmental groups, but by the Department for Transport. For decades, government ministers have told us that airport expansion is essential for “growth”. As chancellor, Rachel Reeves claimed that a third runway at Heathrow would add 0.43% to GDP… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: As Hong Kong heats up, calls grow for tougher rules to protect outdoor workers

item.title: Bushfire simulation reveals green strategy that could cut Australia's fire threat
item.description: New modeling shows irrigating low-flammability vegetation substantially reduces the predicted spread and intensity of wildfires, which could give communities critical extra preparation time, according to a University of the Sunshine Coast study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Los precios de los alimentos se disparan un 5,8 % en un año afectados por las guerras y el clima
item.description: La economía no entiende de negacionismos. Las guerras Ucrania e Irán y las sequías están haciendo estragos: el maíz sube un 5,6 %, el azúcar un 6,1 %, y el trigo un 6,3 %. La producción mundial de cereales caerá un 2,1 % este año y el comercio un 3,5 %, con El Niño amenazando además las cosechas de arroz en Asia. Fuente: Noticias ONU.

item.title: Study links hurricane exposure to higher eviction risk for renters
item.description: Hurricanes can displace renters even when their homes suffer no damage, according to new research led by Rowan University urban planner Qian He. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: El país enfrenta una crisis marcada por las consecuencias prolongadas de la incertidumbre, el desplazamiento y el impacto emocional acumulado sobre los sobrevivientes y rescatistas. item.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding
item.description: Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn. Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. item.title: Increased air pollution linked to more night-time coughing, UK-led study finds
item.description: ‘Day-to-day’ symptom of harmful emissions, which in turn can disrupt sleep, can be overlooked, say researchers New research has found that increased air pollution is associated with more night-time coughing, leading to disturbed sleep. Most air pollution research looks at symptoms that are severe enough for people to seek medical help, but day-to-day symptoms can be overlooked. Prof Cecilia Mascolo, who led the study from the University of Cambridge, said: “I come from an area in Italy with very high pollution and I am very aware of its not-talked-about effects.” Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
